Web finds:
I found 9 usable entries, but the search was thin. Only **4 are clearly from the last 7 days** (Nov 13 to 20). The rest are 2 to 4 weeks old or have no date, and I've marked them. Most numbers come from news or trend sites, not the posts themselves. I didn't open a single original video, so check each one in the app before picking.

**Inside the 7-day window**

- **Workers cheering on the Microsoft 365 outage (about Nov 13, X / Instagram / TikTok, many creators).** Outlook, Teams and Copilot were down for more than a day. Employees posted videos telling the company to "take your time" and spend time with family. A viral post said nobody should come back until January, and others pushed it to March. People called it an "adult snow day". No view counts were given. Shared because every office worker felt it at once: the tool broke and nobody wanted it fixed. **Best fit for OFFICE WITH AI.** The escalating return date matches our twin's "Till March." We can't name the company, but "work tools are down" stands on its own. Sources: [Euro Weekly News, Nov 13](https://euroweeklynews.com/2026/11/13/take-your-time-workers-celebrate-microsoft-outage-with-hilarious-online-reactions/), [ThePrint](https://theprint.in/feature/microsoft-global-outage-meme-fest-circle-back-in-january/3097787/), [Siasat](https://www.siasat.com/no-rush-micro-take-your-time-employees-react-to-outlook-outage-3576648), [Boston Globe](https://www.bostonglobe.com/2026/11/13/metro/microsoft-outage-internet-memes-guffaw/), [Windows Latest](https://www.windowslatest.com/2026/11/14/microsoft-is-begging-you-not-to-blame-ai-for-the-microsoft-365-outage-insisting-it-was-a-botched-network-upgrade/).
- **A toddler who sits his pet goat down to watch reels (Nov 14, Instagram, a mum's account; the article doesn't name her).** Over 371.4K likes and 4.1K comments, per Asianet Newsable. The mum shared her screen-time struggle, and the toddler pulled in the goat to watch reels with him. Shared because it's a gentle, relatable picture of kids and phones. **Possible MUM VS AI** with the roles flipped (Mum and her phone, the committee "joining in"). Source: [Asianet Newsable](https://newsable.asianetnews.com/india/toddler-ropes-in-pet-goat-to-watch-reels-together-as-mom-shares-screen-time-struggle-online-viral-video-articleshow-h2ip00l).
- **A skit where ChatGPT and Gemini give wildly different advice to the same questions (about 4 days old, TikTok).** The search summary didn't give a creator or numbers. It's the AI-contrast shape that worked for us before. Our bible retired "same prompt, 3 AIs", though, so it only works if it's built around one real task. I couldn't confirm how viral it was. Source: [TikTok tag page](https://www.tiktok.com/discover/google-gemini-vs-chat-gpt-meme).
- **"Huss", the new slang (Know Your Meme editorial, Nov 19, TikTok).** The word means sprinting or going all out, and it's used in "In this town everybody goes out partying" memes. No numbers. A weak fit, unless Codex taking a slang word literally is a joke you want. Source: [Know Your Meme](https://knowyourmeme.com/editorials/guides/what-does-huss-mean-the-viral-slang-term-and-in-this-town-everybody-goes-out-partying-memes-explained).

**Older, but the formats are still running**

- **"I Got So Mad" (TikTok, started in late October and took off in early November).** People tell absurd stories of what they did when angry, often with fake or AI-edited photos as "proof". It has moved on to image memes of impossible feats of strength. No numbers were given. Shared for the escalating ridiculous claim. **This fits our "made-up proof" truth:** an AI inventing evidence with total confidence. Source: [Know Your Meme](https://trending.knowyourmeme.com/editorials/guides/whats-the-i-got-so-mad-meme-the-viral-trend-about-absurd-ways-to-express-anger-explained).
- **"Hi, I was just born" typed into Google's AI Overviews (TikTok, since Aug 2026).** The AI earnestly welcomes the newborn to the world. The first known post (@chudlife31) passed 410K views and 50.6K likes, and a Spanish version in late October passed 1M views. Shared because the AI takes an obvious joke completely seriously. **This is pure "AI being AI"**: Claude's over-earnest welcome, Gemini telling the family. Source: [meme.com](https://meme.com/memes/hi-i-was-just-born).
- **The ChatGPT "fake goodbye" (TikTok, creator Alexandra Cross, around October).** A user says goodbye before deleting the app, and the AI answers with a long, emotional farewell. An X repost passed 14M views, and she later said it was a trend bit. Shared for the clingy, wordy AI reply. **This is basically Claude's character**, but it's at least 4 weeks old. Source: [pasqualepillitteri.it](https://pasqualepillitteri.it/en/news/19857/chatgpt-fake-goodbye-viral-tiktok).
- **JJ Kirwan answering scam calls on his mum's old landline (Instagram and TikTok, KYM editorial Nov 5, so about 15 days old).** He plays along in an over-the-top old-time British accent. The search summary said about 10.2M Instagram views and 4.9M TikTok views in six days, but the KYM page itself only says "millions" and its view counter showed 0. Commenters quoted his lines and screenshotted his faces. Shared because scam calls are a common pain and turning the tables feels good. **A good fit for a scam episode** (an AI committee answering the scammer). Sources: [Know Your Meme](https://trending.knowyourmeme.com/editorials/man-turns-scam-calls-into-comedy-gold-by-answering-his-moms-old-fashioned-telephone-like-its-the-roaring-twenties).
- **A grandmother's voice chat with ChatGPT about her grandson "wanting to marry" it (Instagram, India, no date).** Netizens called it one of the funniest uses of AI, and the comments praised how innocent grandparents are. No numbers. Fits MUM VS AI, but I couldn't confirm it's recent. Source: [Zee News](https://zeenews.india.com/india/my-grandson-wants-to-marry-you-grandmother-s-heartfelt-conversation-with-chatgpt-goes-viral-watch-2963243.html).

**Skipped under the show's rules:** the Jensen Huang affair AI memes (a real person's private life), celebrity look-alike AI parodies (real people), a "banned from ChatGPT" clip about overthrowing a government (political), a taco-shop "seductive dance" skit (440K likes, but suggestive), and a TikTok calling out men (about a group). The Nov 11 reel of a woman giving Diwali gifts to delivery workers (3M+ likes) is heartwarming rather than funny and falls outside the window.

**My pick for tomorrow:** the outage. It's the only clearly in-window, widely covered, relatable office moment, and it remakes as OFFICE WITH AI with no keyword. If you'd rather do an AI-behaviour episode, "Hi, I was just born" or the fake goodbye are the cleanest "yes, mine does that" premises, but both are older.

remakes.creator: Futtyball
remakes.numbers: 3.3M views in about 3 days, 793x the channel's normal, 45.8K views per hour, 90.8K likes, 505 comments
remakes.what_happens: A short AI-made comedy clip. A kid tries a bold move on his mum, talking back to her, and it is over instantly. He does not even get to finish.
remakes.why_it_worked: Everyone knows the moment when standing up to your mum fails at once. Commenters quoted the talk-back line, joked about what their own mums would do ('I would wake up inside a coffin'), and pointed at the speed of it: 'didn't even finish'.
remakes.our_twist: We keep the shape: a confident attempt to stand up to Mum, built up with care, then flattened in one move. In our version it is the AIs who 'help', in true AI ways: therapy-speak essays, a calendar slot nobody asked for, a literal mute. The defeat is gentle and very desi: Mum just calls from Papa's phone. Nobody gets hurt, and the punchline lands on Meera's tired 'Hi, Mum.' There is no violence and none of the original's lines, title or characters.
